Look at the top of this page: the coloured chips (*Reading*, *7 min*) and the box with objectives. None of that is written in the page body. It is all drawn from the front matter.

## The front matter

````markdown
---
title: "Anatomy of a lesson"
description: "One sentence. Shown on the home page and in search."
minutes: 7
kind: read          # read | code | quiz | lab
objectives:
  - "Write a lesson's front matter"
  - "Choose a lesson kind and time estimate"
---
````

| Field | Used for |
|---|---|
| `title` | Page title, sidebar entry, home page row |
| `description` | Subtitle and the grey line under the row on the home page |
| `minutes` | The time chip, the module total and the course total |
| `kind` | The icon and colour: **read**, **code**, **quiz** or **lab** |
| `objectives` | The "By the end of this lesson you will" box |

::: {.callout-important}
## `minutes` switches the header on
The header is only drawn on pages that define `minutes`. Module overview pages omit it on purpose.
:::

## A good lesson shape

1. **Objectives** (from front matter).
2. A short opening that says *why* this matters.
3. One idea per `##` heading. Each heading becomes an entry in the right-hand outline.
4. A **Check your understanding** section with one to three questions.
5. A `.takeaways` block with two to four bullets.

```{=html}
<div class="sm-discuss">
  <p class="sm-discuss-label"><i class="fa-solid fa-comments"></i>Discuss first</p>
  <p>If you could only keep three bullets of this lesson, which would they be? Hold that thought: it is exactly what goes in the takeaways box.</p>
</div>
```

## Check your understanding

```{=html}
<div class="sm-quiz" data-quiz="fitb" data-answer="minutes">
  <p class="sm-quiz-q"><strong>Q1.</strong> Which front matter field turns the lesson header on?</p>
  <div class="sm-quiz-fitb-row">
    <input type="text" class="sm-quiz-blank" placeholder="field name" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
  </div>
  <button class="sm-quiz-check">Check Answer</button>
  <div class="sm-quiz-feedback"></div>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaways}
- Front matter drives the header, time estimates and the home page.
- `kind` is one of read, code, quiz or lab.
- Keep one idea per heading and end with a quiz and takeaways.
:::
